title: Narrowband mixer opens with every channel weight at 0.00, i.e. a palette that renders black
what_happened: With Ha, OIII and SII masters present the mixer opens labelled 'Custom mix' with all nine R/G/B weights at 0.00. Applying that state would map every channel to zero.
expected: When the resolved channel set is Ha+OIII+SII, default to SHO; when it is Ha+OIII only, default to HOO; when it is a single narrowband master, default that channel to a luminance mapping. A user should never have to make three clicks to get out of a state that cannot produce an image.
repro: 1. Seed Ha/OIII/SII masters. 2. Session Review > Workbench > Narrowband mixer. 3. Read the nine weight values and the 'Custom mix' label.
proposed_fix: Initialise _palette/_weights from the best-matching preset for widget.channels in initState/didUpdateWidget instead of 'custom' + zeros.

title: The 'AstroBin' export produces JSON + Markdown, not the acquisition CSV AstroBin imports, and omits the observation date entirely
what_happened: Pressing 'AstroBin' asks for one filename and then writes two sibling files with its own extensions -- rsr-astrobin.json and rsr-astrobin.md -- ignoring the .csv extension I typed. The JSON is {subjectType, integrationSecs, integrationHms, frames, perFrameExposureSecs, title, filter} and the Markdown is a four-line summary. AstroBin's acquisition importer takes a CSV whose columns are date, number, duration, filter, binning, gain, sensorCooling, darks, flats, bias, bortle, meanSqm, meanFwhm, temperature. Neither exported file can be imported; the user has to retype the numbers into AstroBin's form. The export also has no `date` field at all, and AstroBin requires a date on every acquisition row.
expected: Emit AstroBin's acquisition CSV (long-exposure format) with the session date filled in from the stack's frames, so the button does what its name promises: one file the user drops into AstroBin's importer. Keep the Markdown as a secondary 'copy for a forum post' output if desired, and honour the extension the user chose in the save dialog.
repro: 1. Stack result > 'AstroBin'. 2. Save as /tmp/ns-audit/rsr-astrobin.csv. 3. ls -> rsr-astrobin.json and rsr-astrobin.md exist; the .csv does not.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_share_export_service.dart:367 buildAstroBinMetadata (no date field on AstroBinExportMetadata); the two-file write in the same service.
proposed_fix: Add `date` (from the earliest/latest frame captured_at) and emit CSV as the primary format.

title: The stack result can only leave the app as 8-bit PNG/JPEG -- there is no linear FITS or 16-bit TIFF export
what_happened: The stack result screen offers exactly four actions: Export PNG, Export JPEG, Share Card, AstroBin. Export PNG writes an 8-bit RGBA PNG (verified: 512x512, bit depth 8, colour type 6) of the STF-stretched view; Export JPEG writes an 8-bit JPEG. The integrated data itself -- which the engine holds as u16 and which the app already persists as a raw buffer for the viewer -- can never be taken out of Skotiq.
expected: A 'Save FITS' (32-bit float or 16-bit, unstretched, with the acquisition header) or 16-bit TIFF action. Every user of NINA, SGP or the ASIAIR takes the integration into PixInsight, Siril, APP or Photoshop for the actual processing; an 8-bit screen-stretched PNG is a preview, not a deliverable. As shipped, Stack & Share is a dead end: the app is the only place the stack can live.
repro: 1. Complete a Stack & Share run. 2. Read the four buttons in the header; there is no other export surface. 3. `drive_linux.py tree` on the result screen lists exactly: Export PNG, Export JPEG, Share Card, AstroBin, and the Stretch dropdown.
proposed_fix: Add 'Save FITS' writing the unstretched integration with EXPTIME = total integration, STACKCNT, FILTER and the acquisition keywords; the native side already writes FITS elsewhere.

title: The Submit-discovery dialog defaults to TNS -- the live, irreversible, public submission -- rather than a local file export
what_happened: The dialog opens with the TNS chip selected and the primary action reading 'Submit to TNS', with the footnote 'Submits live to the TNS via your bot API key -- creates a public AT record.' AAVSO and MPC, which write a file to disk that the user uploads themselves, are the non-default options.
expected: Default to the reversible action. The first-listed and pre-selected network should be a local export (AAVSO), with TNS an explicit opt-in -- creating a public Astronomical Transient record on a mis-classified residual is not undoable, and a first-time user reaching this dialog has by definition never submitted anything before.
repro: 1. Analytics > Science > First Light > Submit on any confirmed candidate. 2. Read which chip is selected and what the primary button says.
proposed_fix: Initialise _format to the first ENABLED format, preferring aavso > mpc > tns; if none is enabled, select aavso and show its (cheapest) blocker.

title: An unrecognised transient-kind token is presented to the user as a definite 'Dipole' artefact classification, which also silently blocks submission
what_happened: TransientKind.fromWire falls back to TransientKind.dipole for any token it does not recognise. The candidate card then renders a 'Dipole' chip -- a specific, factual claim about the residual's morphology -- and Submit refuses with 'Dipole artefacts are not real transients - they cannot be submitted.' I hit this with a row whose kind was 'new_source' instead of the wire token 'newSource': the card asserted the detection was a dipole artefact and would not let it be reported. The fallback is deliberate and documented ('the least-exciting, artefact-leaning class'), but the UI presents the fallback as a measurement.
expected: Keep the conservative gating, but label it honestly: an unknown token should render as 'Unclassified' and the refusal message should read 'This detection has an unrecognised classification and cannot be submitted', not assert a dipole morphology the differencing code never reported.
repro: 1. Insert a transient_detections row with kind='new_source'. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light. 3. The card shows a 'Dipole' chip; pressing Submit toasts 'Dipole artefacts are not real transients - they cannot be submitted.' 4. Change kind to 'newSource' and restart -> the same row now reads 'New source' and Submit opens the dialog.
proposed_fix: Add an `unknown` member to TransientKind, make fromWire return it, label it 'Unclassified', and gate submission on `kind == newSource || kind == pointBrightening || kind == movingStreak` rather than on `!= dipole`.

title: The five-rung Science guide is a set of paragraphs, not a ladder you can climb -- every rung opens an explanation and a 'Got it' button with no action
what_happened: Analytics > Science shows a 'Science guide' with rungs 1-5 (Measure your sky / Track a star / Build a light curve / Find the period / Contribute it) and a single page-level 'Run calibration' button. Opening rung 2 gives 'Point at a target and let the photometry follow it frame to frame...' plus the gate 'Calibrate your sky first so brightness reads true.' and one button: 'Got it'. Rung 5 gives 'Your measurements are good enough to share...' plus 'Find a period - or build out the curve - before exporting.' and again only 'Got it'. Neither sheet offers the action it is describing, or a link to where that action lives. The only actionable rung is rung 1, whose button is on the page rather than in the sheet.
expected: Each rung sheet should carry the action for that rung -- 'Pick a target' (rung 2), 'Open the light curve' (rung 3), 'Run period search' (rung 4), 'Open the export hub' (rung 5) -- enabled or disabled with the stated prerequisite. As built, a user who reads the ladder has to go find each surface themselves, which is exactly the discoverability problem the ladder exists to solve.
repro: 1. Analytics > Science. 2. Click rung 2 'Track a star' -> sheet with text and 'Got it'. 3. Escape, click rung 5 'Contribute it' -> sheet with text and 'Got it'.
proposed_fix: Give ScienceRungSheet a primary action per rung that routes to that rung's surface, disabled with the prerequisite as its tooltip when the gate is unmet.
